Таким образом, реинжиниринг бизнес-процессов является необходимым инструментом для компаний, которые хотят успешно соперничать на рынке. Он позволяет быстро и эффективно адаптироваться к новым условиям, улучшить качество продукции, сократить затраты и повысить мотивацию сотрудников. Однако, перед тем как приступать к реинжинирингу бизнес-процессов, компании должны оценить необходимость и подготовиться к этому процессу.

整理各国在太空交通管理方面提出的政策、论文、设想等，例如美国、欧洲、俄罗斯、日本、中国、印度等。各国对太空交通管理的态度是怎么样的？预期形成什么样的太空交通管理模式？联合国等国际组织在太空交通管理方面有什么建议。美国SSC提出的最佳太空行为实践指南，对实现太空交通管理有什么帮助？

1. 美国：美国政府非常重视太空交通管理。2010年发布的全国航天政策要求美国国家航天局(NASA)和国防部(DoD)合作开发一个太空交通管理系统，确保安全、有效地利用近地轨道空间。2019年，特朗普政府发布《太空交通管理政策》，规定政府内部机构的合作和负责范围。美国商业航天公司SpaceX也开发了一款名为“Starlink”的卫星互联网系统，有效减少碰撞风险和提高太空交通管理的效率。美国太空体系司令部（SSC）提出的最佳太空行为实践指南将有助于进一步提高太空交通安全性并遵守国际义务。

2. 欧洲：欧洲太空总署（ESA）于2017年发布了《欧洲太空交通管理倡议书》，提出建立一个太空交通管理系统，目的是确保各国太空行为的安全和有效。并在2020年发布了《欧洲太空交通管理制度研究》文件，为建立一个有效的、可持续的太空交通管理制度提供基本框架。此外，ESA和空中客车联手开发“Space Tug”，该项目致力于减少太空碎片、降低碰撞风险并改善太空交通管理。

3. 俄罗斯：俄罗斯一直在与其他国家合作开展太空交通管理经验，提高国际太空安全性。俄罗斯与美国在2015年至2017年间共同发起了国际空间碎片协调会议，讨论开展太空碎片清除任务。2019年，俄罗斯政府同意参加联合国“长期太空可持续发展”倡议，以改善空间领域法律和规章制度。

4. 日本：日本政府已确定太空交通管理为国家战略目标，并在2018年发布《太空碎片风险管理综合战略》。此外，日本航空航天研究机构（JAXA）加入了“太空格局观测部署计划”，参与对轨道空间的监测，对太空交通安全贡献力量。

5. 中国：中国政府已经认识到太空交通管理的重要性。2015年，中国与俄罗斯共同提交了《防止部署武器进入外层空间元首声明》，强调太空武器化的安全风险，并提出建立一个透明、开放的太空交通管理制度。近年来，中国的太空技术发展迅速，已初步具备了自主发展、运营太空交通管理系统的能力。

6. 印度：印度政府在2020年成立了国家太空推广和授权中心（IN-SPACe）来推动印度太空产业的发展。印度与许多国家和国际组织合作，加强太空碎片的探测和预警。印度空间研究组织（ISRO）已经制定了一项关于轨道道路网的设计概念，帮助降低卫星碰撞的风险。

7. 联合国：联合国积极推动国际间在太空交通管理上的合作。商定国际太空法律框架，提出建立全球太空面貌观测系统。联合国大会于2018年通过了《防止太空冲突和长期太空可持续发展》决议草案，增强各国在太空交通安全方面的合作意识。

美国SSC提出的最佳太空行为实践指南，对实现太空交通管理的帮助包括：

1.提高国际合作和共识，促进各国根据国际空间规范进行太空行为。

2.强调太空行为的透明度和可预测性，降低太空冲突的风险。

3.推动共享太空监测和环境数据，帮助各国预防和应对威胁，提高太空交通管理能力。

4.鼓励与商业和民间行业合作，形成多元化的太空交通管理系统。

Deliverables
You will upload to Canvas a single .zip file, titled LastNameFirstInit_Lab8.zip, containing two separate files: 1) LastNameFirstInit_Lab8.m will contain your ABM3 code in response to Task 1, and 2) LastNameFirstInit_Lab8.pdf will contain your lab report in response to Task 2.

Terminology
State Variables
In a dynamical system (such as an Initial Value Problem), the dependent variables are also called the state variables. e.g., in Problem 5 of HW #9, x and v (or ẋ) are the state variables. These variables are often put into an array, which is called the state array. While the independent variable (usually time, for us) is not technically considered a state variable, we are primarily interested in the system state as a function of time. In our case, we will insert the independent variable as the first value in the state array and call it the augmented state array.

Mode Shapes and Natural Frequencies
Consider the vibration system below. As a two degree of freedom system, it has two natural frequencies and two mode shapes. If the two masses are both displaced to the left (by the correct distances) and released, they will each undergo perfect sinusoidal motion. Both will oscillate at the same frequency – called the first natural frequency. The first mode shape is a normalized vector representing respective signed amplitudes of their oscillations. The second mode shape and second natural frequency occur when the two masses are released after being displaced (by the correct distances) in opposite directions. In this case, the values in the mode shapes will have different signs, because the masses are moving in opposite directions.

Task #1
Write a single function script to perform the Third Order Adams-Bashforth-Moulton algorithm on a system of ordinary differential equations (IVP). The program must be able to handle any number of differential equations (an IVP with any number of state variables).
Your function m-file will receive through its header the following problem parameters (in this
exact order):
a. a cell array containing the function handles of the equations describing the time derivatives of the several state variables
b. the initial augmented state-array – a numerical row array containing the needed starting values of the independent variable and the several state variables (in the same order as the function handles in the cell array from the first input argument)
c. the step size to be used, and
d. the number of steps to take

Function Output
Your file should not return anything to the calling program. Instead, it should
i. print to screen (the command window) the final state of the system, including t, and
ii. plot a trace for each of the dependent variables as a function of time.
Plot each trace on a separate graph. To facilitate plotting, store the results of all time steps in the augmented state-array
a. each row represents the system at a different point in time
b. column 1 contains the time, and each other column contains the temporal history of a particular state variable
Store only the final result of each time step, not the predicted or non-converged corrected values. Title each plot ‘Var1’, ‘Var2’, etc. Try help plot and help title in the MATLAB command window to learn more about plotting. num2str will also be useful for creating the labels themselves.

Hints for your Function Script
Handling a System of Un-predetermined Size
Technical
Because you will not know in advance the order of the IVP your function will be asked to solve, some of the system parameters will need to be passed in as arrays, rather than as scalars. The step size and number of steps will still be scalars, but there will be an un-predetermined number of state variables, each of which will have an associated starting value and derivative expression. The starting value of each state variable is a scalar, so the collection of them can be stored in a normal array. On the other hand, your function script must be passed a separate function handle for the equation for the time derivative of each state variable. To store function handles, we must use a cell array. So then, you must be able to evaluate a function handle stored in a cell array. We did this in Lab #4, but I cover it again later in this document.
NOTE: Because your augmented state array will include time as the first value, the function stored in the nth index of the cell array is actually the derivative of the state variable in the (n+1)th index of the augmented state array.

Metaphysical
To figure out how to structure your code to deal with any size system, consult HW#9 and the notes from lab. In the HW, we performed RK3 on a 2nd order system. We can call the state variables x and v, and we can call their slopes (time derivatives) k and m, respectively. Feel free to write out and logically group the steps you took to solve the system for one timestep. Now, imagine we have 3 or 4 state variables each with their own slopes. Again, write out and logically group the steps you took to solve the system of equations. What changed about the process? Did the number of groups increase? Did the number of steps within particular groups increase? Now, we need to replace the RK3 algorithm steps with the ABM3 algorithm steps. Pay careful attention to the following differences:
a. the predictor and its modifier are performed once per time step, the corrector and its modifier are repeated until convergence each time step
b. the is no modifier on the predictor in the first time step
c. when performing the modifier steps, you use only non-modified values
d. when you check for convergence you compare only modified values

Function handles with unknown number of inputs
If you remember doing this for Modified Secant on a system of equations, then you may skip this section.
Up to now, you’ve probably only used function handles for equations that had a predetermined number of inputs. For this program, each derivative equation may be a function of the independent variable and any or all of the state variables. This is only a problem because you don’t know now (as you’re writing the function script) how many or which of the state variables will appear in each of the derivative equations. Fortunately, MATLAB allows us to put arrays into the equation function evaluation.
For example, if I define a function handle:
d1_by_dt = @(t,a) a(1) * a(3) / (2 + t);
when you ask MATLAB to evaluate the mathematical expression, MATLAB will expect to receive a scalar as the 1st argument, and an array of at least three terms as the 2nd argument. It will use the first and third terms in the array, along with the scalar, to evaluate the expression.
The augmented state array passed into the function already has t as the first value, so let’s just stick with that. Then our example equation becomes:
d1_by_dt = @(a) a(2) * a(4) / (2 + a(1));
You, of course, will have no prior knowledge of which state variables are used in each derivative expression. Therefore, for each derivative evaluation, you will need to submit an array containing the correct values of the dependent variable and all of the state variables, in the same order as the initial values in the passed-in augmented state array. When grading your code, it will be my responsibility to ensure that all of the derivative equations use the correct variables.

Function handles in cell arrays
The function handles of the derivative expressions of the several state variables will be passed to your function script in a cell array. The syntax for evaluating a function handle that is stored in a cell array is as follows:
value = array_name{n}(input1, input2, ... , inputQ)
• array_name is the name of the cell array in which the handles are stored
• n is the index into the cell array, in which is stored the expression for (d/dt)y n
• input1 thru inputQ are the inputs to the mathematical expression represented by the function handle – in our case that will simply be the augmented state array
Please note that those are braces around the index ‘n’ and parentheses around the arguments.

The ABM3 process
To calculate the predicted value of each state variable, you are going to perform very similar math:
n+1 ^0y k = n y k + h((23/12)g ^k n - (4/3)g^k n-1 + (5/12)g^k n-2)

where the k superscript on each g term matches the state variable number (the k subscript on each y term). Take advantage of how MATALB deals with vectors to simplify the process of calculating the predictor for all the state variable and each subsequent corrector for all the state variables. Create an array that holds the g m evaluations for all of the state variables. You will have 3 or 4 of these, one for each timestep. Then you can ...
temp_state = current_state + (h / 2) * slopes_array

Test your program
The spring-mass system from the Terminology section has been reproduced here.
Neglecting friction, the equations of motion of this system are:
ẍ1 = (-(k1+k2)x1 + k2x2)/m1
ẍ2 = (-(k2+k3)x2 + k2x1)/m2

where x1 and x2 are measured from the static equilibrium locations of the respective masses. To handle the 2nd order nature of the time derivatives, we must include additional state variables v1 and v2. If we arrange the state variables in the order x1, v1, x2, v2, the augmented state array becomes t, x1, v1, x2, v2, and the corresponding differential equations becomes:
dx1/dt = g1(a) = a(3)
dv1/dt = g2(a) = (-(k1+k2)a(2) + k2a(4))/m1
dx2/dt = g3(a) = a(5)
dv2/dt = g4(a) = (-(k2+k3)a(4) + k2a(2))/m2

Remember, a(1) is time, which does not appear in our equations of motion.

When you find the correct value of x2(0) each mass should demonstrate smooth sinusoidal motion. Inspect your table of state variables to determine the period of the oscillation. The period is the time between consecutive maximum displacements. The frequency in Hz is the inverse of the period. The mode shape is the vector [x1(0); x2(0)] scaled to have a Euclidean norm of unity (1).
Include in your Lab Report the following:

% In the code below:
%
% g is cell array containing the various dy/dt functions
%
% s_a is the augmented state array. It starts out as a row vector. It is
% passed in with the starting values of t and each state variable, in the
% same order as the function handles in the g cell array.  It will
% eventually contain all of the values of t and the state variables over
% time.
%
% h is the step size

N = length(g);
slopes = zeros(4,N)

for iter = 1:2
    state = s_a(iter,:);
    for c = 1:N
        slopes(1,c) = g{c}(state);
    end
    
    state = s_a(iter,:) + (h/2)*[1, slopes(1,:)];
    for c = 1:N
        slopes(2,c) = g{c}(state);
    end
    
    state = s_a(iter,:) + (h/2)*[1, slopes(2,:)];
    for c = 1:N
        slopes(3,c) = g{c}(state);
    end
    
    state = s_a(iter,:) + h*[1, slopes(3,:)];
    for c = 1:N
        slopes(4,c) = g{c}(state);
    end
    
    RK = (slopes(1,:) + 2*slopes(2,:) + 2*slopes(3,:) + slopes(4,:)) / 6;
    
    s_a(iter+1,:) = s_a(iter,:) + h*[1, RK]

Hier ist ein einfaches und leckeres Rezept für Pasta mit Zucchini:

Zutaten:
- 400 g Nudeln (z.B. Penne oder Spaghetti)
- 2 Zucchini
- 2 Knoblauchzehen
- 1/2 Zwiebel
- 4 EL Olivenöl
- Salz und Pfeffer
- Parmesan oder Pecorino zum Servieren

Zubereitung:
1. Die Nudeln nach Packungsanweisung in reichlich Salzwasser al dente kochen.
2. In der Zwischenzeit die Zucchini waschen und in kleine Würfel schneiden.
3. Die Knoblauchzehen schälen und fein hacken. Die Zwiebel ebenfalls schälen und in kleine Stücke schneiden.
4. In einer Pfanne das Olivenöl erhitzen und die Zwiebel und den Knoblauch darin glasig dünsten.
5. Die Zucchinistücke in die Pfanne geben und bei mittlerer Hitze 5-7 Minuten braten, bis sie weich und goldbraun sind.
6. Die Nudeln abgießen und zusammen mit den Zucchini in die Pfanne geben. Alles gut vermengen und mit Salz und Pfeffer abschmecken.
7. Mit Parmesan oder Pecorino servieren.

Guten Appetit!

Title: Tips for Staying Safe in Morocco: Wander with Confidence

Introduction

Morocco, an enchanting land of colorful souks, fragrant spices, and captivating landscapes, has long been a favorite destination for travelers worldwide. This stunning North African country has much to offer - from bustling cities like Marrakech and Casablanca to idyllic beaches and magical deserts. However, it's essential always to remain vigilant and prioritize personal safety while enjoying the sights and sounds of this lovely nation. This engaging and constructive article offers tips and tricks for staying safe in Morocco, letting you embrace your surroundings without any concerns while fostering rich, lifelong memories.

1. Dress Appropriately and Respectfully

Morocco is a predominantly Muslim nation with conservative attire notions, especially when visiting sacred spaces. Dressing modestly helps maintain cultural respect and reduces the chances of attracting unwelcome attention. Aim to cover your shoulders, chest, and knees, and ladies may also wish to carry a headscarf for added discretion.

2. Be Confident and Assertive

Moroccan markets and medinas thrive with energy and excitement but can sometimes be overwhelming for first-time visitors. Shopkeepers may call out to you enticingly. Having an assertive and confident demeanor may aid in navigating crowded streets and fending off persistent sellers. A courteous refusal or a polite "La, shukran" (No, thank you) should suffice.

3. Beware of ''Friendly'' Locals and False Guides

While Moroccans generally possess a reputation for warmth and hospitality, be cautious about accepting offers from unofficial guides, as some may lead you to undesirable situations or charge exorbitant fees. Select guides recommended by your hotel or accredited by the Ministry of Tourism to ensure a pleasant experience.

4. Safeguard Your Belongings

Thoroughly research your accommodations in advance, as reliable safety measures could vary. It's wise to secure valuable items in a room safe or lock them in your suitcase. Additionally, refrain from carrying excessive cash or flashing expensive jewelry in public. Opt for a stylish money belt or cross-body bag for easy access to essentials and added security.

5. Choose Taxis and Public Transportation Wisely

Traveling through Morocco via taxis or public transportation may seem daunting initially. Hire registered petits or grands taxis, prominently displaying their licenses and registration cards, to ensure a secure trip. When taking buses or trains, keep your belongings within view and reach.

6. Mind Your Food and Water

Though Moroccan cuisine is undeniably delicious, maintaining your health while traveling is vital. Opt for cooked meals and bottled or purified water to minimize the risk of food poisoning or water-borne diseases. Street food, though tantalizing, may not always be safe for consumption.

7. Keep Track of Emergency Contacts

Get acquainted with local emergency phone numbers, and have them saved on your phone or noted in a secure place. Ensure your travel companions, family members, or friends back home are aware of your whereabouts and intended travel plans.

8. Exercise Caution When Using ATMs

ATMs are typically secure in Morocco, but being cautious is never amiss. Use machines at established banks during business hours or within well-lit areas to avoid compromising your financial details. It's also vital to monitor your transactions and report any discrepancies immediately.

Conclusion

Morocco is a treasure trove of vibrant culture and unforgettable experiences. Taking extra precautions and following our safety tips should help circumvent potential issues, allowing you to fully immerse yourself in the beauty of this captivating country. Embrace the adventure, and wander with confidence, knowing that you're well-prepared for a trip of a lifetime. Happy and safe travels await you in the enchanting land of Morocco!

Given the mature and challenging insurance market environment, “combatting fraud has become an important factor for success in the competition with other insurers,” noted Lanzoni.

Within personal lines of insurance, the majority of fraud takes quite a mundane shape and is therefore difficult to uncover. There’s a well-known correlation, for example, between the launch of next-generation flatscreen TVs right before large sporting events (i.e. soccer World Cups) and a concurrent spike in claims for broken or stolen units. The German GDV also analysed claims that arose from lost or damaged smartphones and concluded that close to 50 per cent could not possibly have happened. Combatting this type of fraud is burdensome, but if the same person who just reported their mobile lphone theft pops up across data bases with suspicious activities, a red flag could be raised so that a claims expert can have a closer look.

HDI Seguros in Brazil has invested into the Anti-Fraud Platform provided by SAS to do just that. The models which combine text mining, predictive analytics and machine learning are expected to result in a “marked decrease of false positives and an increase of 25 per cent in suspected fraud cases”, explains Luiz Novaes, Systems Manager at HDI Seguros. The platform is also improving the efficiency of the overall claims process.
 

Commercial insurances: AI could help reduce premiums in the future
Industrial insurances require a slightly different approach. Gathering data for complex analyses is not as straightforward as in private insurances. Detecting fraud on a corporate level would require tapping into a variety of sources such as corporate reporting, official filings, director searches, legal judgment data, and credit ratings.

HDI, however, focusses instead on protecting clients from criminal activities. Detecting attempted fraud by customers or employees could help to significantly reduce costs in some industries  – and thereby possibly have a positive effect on insurance premiums.

AI is useful in a variety of industries where a lot of data are available, making it possible to search for patterns. For example, retail chains often face claims from customers who say they have fallen and were injured in a store. Data analysis can find patterns in the claims and point out dubious ones. “When you have multiple cases from addresses, phone numbers, bank accounts, or other data points that show a connection, you may want to investigate them further”, explains HDI expert Thomas Staubach.
 

Possible applications in transportation and workers compensation
“Another area where we see interesting opportunities is transportation – not just regarding fraud, but also for the detection of other crimes”, he says. For example, when a truck and its load are stolen, an analysis of data from similar cases may show that the driver has connections to various other vehicles or containers that have disappeared.

A third strong use case are group accident insurances. For example, workers sometimes blame their employers for injuries that had nothing to do with their job, hoping to collect damages. This potentially increases the employer’s premium, while also having a negative effect on their image as a safe workplace.

“However, all suspicious cases have to be followed up manually before any legal action is taken”, emphasises Staubach.

The only way is forward
Turning such ideas into reality still takes a lot of time. Whether you implement the AI system in-house or cooperate with a third party, setting it up for success is a task of huge proportions. Ultimately, we are talking about automating the extraction of data and recognition of patterns – those known and those that have not yet been uncovered.

The work is worth the potential reward, as for any large insurer with billions in paid-out claims, even a 10 per cent reduction in fraudulent claims can translate into considerable improvements to the bottom line. In their latest study on technology in insurance fraud detection, the Coalition Against Insurance Fraud stated that insurers who “embrace the right mix of tools, staffing, training and technologies”, will see “reduced claims costs, more accurate pricing, a competitive edge and lower premiums for policyholders.” An outcome that is good for everyone.'

This website is intended for an audience outside of the United States.

Solutions & Services

As the insurance industry continues to be hit by fraudulent claims, insurers are increasingly turning to AI and machine learning to identify and prevent fraudulent claims. By tapping into large datasets and cross-referencing data points across various internal databases and external sources, insurers can analyze patterns and identify instances of insurance fraud. The use of AI and machine learning has shown promising results in detecting and combating fraud in various areas, such as transportation, workers compensation, and personal lines of insurance.

Title: Savory Secrets: Top 10 Delicious Moroccan Foods You Cannot Miss

Morocco's culinary landscape is as diverse and vibrant as the country itself. Rich in history, culture and tradition, Moroccan cuisine is an extraordinary fusion of flavors, colors and textures that will excite your taste buds, nourish your senses and leave an indelible mark on your memory. The following 10 mouth-watering foods are must-try delicacies that you simply can't afford to miss during your Moroccan adventure!

1. Couscous

When visiting Morocco, you simply must start with couscous – the national dish, beloved by locals and visitors alike. These tiny steamed balls of semolina are deliciously fluffy and served with a variety of mouth-watering toppings, such as tender meat, aromatic vegetables, and a flavorsome broth. This fulfilling meal represents the heart and soul of Moroccan home-cooking and can be enjoyed at any time of the day.

2. Tagine

The much-loved tagine is more than just a delightful meal; it is a unique cooking technique that showcases Morocco's culinary heritage. Named after the conical earthenware pot in which it is cooked, this slow-cooked stew is the epitome of comfort food. With a plethora of flavors ranging from sweet to spicy and an enchanting variety of ingredients such as lamb, chicken, prunes, and almonds, every tagine is a delightful gastronomic journey.

3. B'stilla

Craving a dish with a perfect balance of sweet and savory? Look no further than b'stilla – Morocco's irresistible answer to the ultimate flavor fusion. Traditionally prepared with pigeon, this indulgent pastry is made up of layers of paper-thin phyllo dough filled with spiced meat, almonds, and eggs, finished with a dusting of sugar and cinnamon. B'stilla's combination of carefully selected flavors and textures make for a heavenly mouthful that melts in your mouth.

4. Harira

For a taste of Morocco's soul, a bowl of steaming hot harira is an absolute must. This wholesome soup is traditionally served to break the fast during the holy month of Ramadan but can be enjoyed at any time of the year. A hearty combination of lentils, chickpeas, tomatoes, and spices create a delicious and deeply satisfying dish that is as nourishing to the body as it is to the mind and soul.

5. Zaalouk

Vegetarians rejoice! Zaalouk is a marvelous Moroccan salad that is bound to tickle your fancy. Prepared with eggplant, tomatoes, garlic, and a blend of spices, this tasty dish is simultaneously smoky, spicy, and refreshing. Served with warm bread or alongside a meaty main course, zaalouk is a truly versatile dish that every traveler should sample.

6. Msemen

These delectable square-shaped Moroccan pancakes are a popular breakfast item and teatime treat. Msemen can be enjoyed both sweet and savory, with various toppings such as honey, cheese, or even minced meat. With their perfectly golden, crispy exterior and delightfully layered and flaky interior, it is near impossible to stop at just one msemen.

7. Kefta

For a flavorful burst of Moroccan spices, kefta (seasoned ground meat) is the dish to sink your teeth into. Traditionally made with lamb or beef, these succulent meatballs are infused with a mouthwatering mix of spices such as paprika, cumin, and coriander. Grilled, fried, or simmered in a rich tomato sauce, kefta dishes leave a lasting impression on your palate.

8. Pastilla au lait

Have a sweet tooth? Pastilla au lait is the delightful dessert you've been craving. This luscious and creamy custard-filled pastry is incredibly satisfying, with its delicate layers of flaky dough wrapped around a milky filling, flavored with orange blossom water and dusted with sugar and cinnamon. It's the perfect way to round off a Moroccan feast – or treat yourself at any time of the day.

9. Briouat

These delightful little pastries offer a taste sensation with every bite. Sweet or savory, briouats are made from phyllo dough, stuffed with a variety of ingredients such as spiced meat, cheese or almonds and honey, and then deep-fried to crispy perfection. Their irresistible crunch and succulent filling make them an ideal snack to be enjoyed on the go or at leisure, over a steaming cup of Moroccan mint tea.

10. Sfenj

Last but certainly not least, sfenj are Morocco's answer to the doughnut. These hand-shaped, deep-fried rings of dough have a delightfully chewy texture that can only be described as addictive. Traditionally enjoyed for breakfast or with afternoon tea, sfenj is best eaten hot and fresh from the fryer, dusted with a little sugar or soaked in honey for maximum indulgence.

Your Moroccan sojourn is incomplete without trying each of these 10 mind-blowing dishes. With tastes, textures, and flavors unlike anything you've ever experienced, Moroccan cuisine is a shining jewel in the crown of world gastronomy. Get ready to embark on the food adventure of a lifetime – Morocco awaits!

You are a world renowned SEO guru for Google with extensive and unrivaled knowledge for making content for students and learning. Write a list of 20 pain points that people learning or studying, suffer from with a minimum of 500 word paragraphs for each pain point that resolve each one.

1. Lack of motivation

A common pain point for people learning or studying is a lack of motivation. This can lead to procrastination, poor time management, and ultimately not retaining the information. To address this issue, it's crucial to set clear goals and visualize the bigger picture. Understanding why you're learning a particular subject and how it'll benefit you in the long run can boost motivation. Additionally, breaking down tasks into smaller chunks and rewarding yourself for reaching milestones can help keep you engaged and committed to your studies.

2. Poor organizational skills

Many learners struggle with organizing their study materials, time, and workload which disrupts their overall productivity. Developing proper organizational skills is key to overcoming this challenge. Creating a study schedule, having a dedicated study space, and using tools like planners and calendars can significantly improve organization. Additionally, regularly decluttering your study space and organizing digital files can help minimize distractions and promote focus.

3. Difficulty concentrating and focusing

Remaining focused and maintaining concentration during long study sessions can be challenging for most people. Employing effective study techniques like the Pomodoro Technique, which involves working in 25-minute intervals followed by a short break, can enhance concentration. Furthermore, eliminating distractions by turning off notifications for phones and computers, using noise-canceling headphones, and setting specific study times will help you stay focused.

4. Struggling with memorization

Retaining information can be a significant pain point for learners. Engaging active learning methods like the Feynman technique, where learners explain concepts in simple terms, and the Cornell note-taking method, involving summarizing and organizing notes, can aid in effective memorization. Adding mnemonic techniques, such as creating associations or acronyms, can further improve information retention.

5. Lack of effective study strategies

Some learners may retain information and understand concepts better through visual cues, while others may benefit from an auditory or kinesthetic style. It's essential to identify which learning style best suits you and employ effective study strategies that incorporate that style. Using flashcards, concept maps, or teaching concepts to others are some ways to personalize your study approach.

6. Feeling overwhelmed by the workload

Learners often face an extensive workload, and handling multiple tasks and deadlines can be daunting. Managing your time effectively and prioritizing tasks can help you feel more in control. Break tasks into smaller components, set specific deadlines for each, and utilize productivity tools like to-do lists and time-blocking methods to maintain a balanced workload.

7. Test anxiety

Exams and assessments can create anxiety and stress for learners, affecting their performance. Adopting stress management techniques like deep breathing exercises, visualizations, and mindfulness meditation can help to alleviate test anxiety. Additionally, practicing good study habits, preparing early for exams, and taking timed practice tests can improve confidence and lower anxiety levels.

8. Lack of proper sleep

Getting adequate sleep is vital for the brain to process and retain information effectively. To ensure proper rest, establish a regular sleep schedule, avoid caffeine and heavy meals before bed, and create a peaceful sleep environment devoid of screens and distractions. Engaging in relaxation techniques, such as progressive muscle relaxation or meditation, can also promote quality sleep.

9. Poor time management

Learners often struggle with managing their time effectively, leading to procrastination and added stress. Incorporating time-management techniques, such as setting deadlines, prioritizing tasks, and using productivity tools like calendars and timers, can help learners stay on top of their work and achieve a better work-study-life balance.

10. Struggling with comprehension

Many learners experience difficulties in understanding complex subjects or concepts. Working with a study buddy, joining a study group, or seeking help from a tutor can provide additional explanations and perspectives that improve comprehension. Also, engaging in critical thinking activities that analyze, apply, and synthesize concepts can strengthen understanding.

11. Difficulty with writing assignments

Writing effective essays or research papers can be challenging for many learners. Developing strong writing skills through consistent practice, using resources like writing centers or online tutorials, and employing revision strategies like peer review and editing checklists can significantly improve writing abilities.

12. Inadequate study resources or materials

The quality of resources can greatly impact the efficiency of learning. It is crucial to identify the most relevant and reliable materials to support your studies. Seek recommendations from teachers, librarians, or peers, and take advantage of online resources such as educational websites, databases, and e-books.

13. Disorganization of digital files

Organizing digital materials effectively is essential for maximizing productivity. Leveraging tools like note-taking and cloud storage apps can help keep digital files well-organized and accessible. Employing naming conventions and file categorization techniques can further streamline organization.

14. Balancing work, school, and personal life

Finding the right balance is crucial for nurturing personal well-being and reducing stress. Establish a routine that accommodates personal, work, and academic commitments. Make time for relaxation, exercise, and hobbies to create a healthy and all-round lifestyle.

15. Managing group projects

Working in groups can be challenging, especially when navigating different personalities and work styles. Establishing clear communication, setting defined roles, and regularly checking on individual and team progress can help foster a productive group dynamic.

16. Weak problem-solving skills

Developing strong problem-solving skills is vital for academic success. Encourage critical thinking, practice with a variety of problems, and approach new challenges with curiosity and resilience. Reflect on mistakes and learn from them, as they serve as valuable opportunities for growth.

17. Limited access to technology

Limited access to proper equipment or online resources can hinder the digital aspects of learning. Seek ways to maximize the available resources or explore affordable alternatives such as refurbished technology, open-access resources, and community resources like public libraries.

18. Lack of interest in the subject matter

Feeling disinterested in the subject matter can hamper motivation and learning. Attempt to create connections between the subject and personal interests, increasing its relevance by exploring its real-world applications. Discussing the subject with peers or conducting further research can also pique interest.

19. Difficulty managing stress

Academics can be a source of stress for many learners. Adopting stress-management techniques, like physical exercise, mindfulness practices, and setting realistic expectations, can help manage stress levels and remain focused on learning.

20. Frustration with setbacks

Overcoming setbacks, such as receiving a low grade or struggling with a concept, can be difficult. Treating setbacks as opportunities for improvement rather than failures is crucial. Seek support to identify areas of growth, make necessary changes, and continue to persevere in your academic journey.

1. iPhone SE (1st and 2nd generation)、iPhone 5s, 5c 和 5 : 建议使用640x1136像素的图片。

4. iPhone X, XS, 和 11 Pro : 建议使用1125x2436像素的图片。

5. iPhone XR, 11 : 建议使用828x1792像素的图片。

6. iPhone XS Max, 11 Pro Max : 建议使用1242x2688像素的图片。

7. iPhone 12 Mini : 建议使用1080x2340像素的图片。

8. iPhone 12, 12 Pro : 建议使用1170x2532像素的图片。

13. 12.9-inch iPad Pro : 建议使用2048x2732像素的图片。

当然，有时不需要为每种尺寸都提供一张图片。您可以使用“@2x”和“@3x”版本的图片资源，并让 iOS 设备适当缩放来展示。例如，为了适应 iPhone 8 和 iPhone 8 Plus，您可以分别准备750x1334像素（@2x）和1242x2208像素（@3x）的图片。

Airflow retry dag with delay

In Airflow, you can configure a DAG to retry failed tasks with a delay between each retry attempt. 

To do this, you need to modify the DAG default_args dictionary and add the following parameters:

- retries: the number of times to retry a failed task (default is 0)
- retry_delay: the delay between retry attempts (default is timedelta(seconds=300))

Here's an example of how to add these parameters to the default_args dictionary:

```
default_args = {
    'owner': 'airflow',
    'depends_on_past': False,
    'start_date': datetime(2021, 12, 1),
    'retries': 3,
    'retry_delay': timedelta(minutes=5),
}
```

Clara Nittmo, known to her contacts as "The Riveting Raven," was well acquainted with this underbelly. Her dyed raven hair and piercing green eyes unsettled even the most hardened of criminals, leaving many wondering if she too had a lingering darkness inside her.

An agent of the organization Obsidian, Clara had managed to infiltrate and disband various rival syndicates. Her newest target, Cesare Romano, went by the innocuous title of 'The Gardener.' To the public, he was a simple botanist and owner of the city's most renowned greenhouse. To the criminal underworld, he commanded a legitimate empire, dealing in underground arms deals and masterminding assassinations.

As Clara pushed open the unassuming door to the greenhouse, she smiled to herself imagining how the rumors of her fearsome reputation made its way through the criminal community.

"Incroyable," she whispered, "You'd never suspect this place was the hub of such dastardly dealings."

The humidity swelled beneath the glass domes, smothering her like a hot summer's day. Colors swirled around her, floral scents flitting through the air. Roses, gardenias, chrysanthemums, and far more exotic blooms filled the space with a sense of extravagant decadence.

Striking foliage mixed with elaborate glass chandeliers, creating a contrast between the natural and artificial beauty. A smattering of metallic tools and machinery glistened through the leaves, drawing attention to the countless trapdoors that led down into The Gardener's hidden lair.

Skulking between the rose bushes, Clara allowed the sensation of danger to play with her nerves. And through that very excitement, she felt alive. Finally, she located Cesare, standing behind a table of exotic orchids he was tending, unaware of her presence. 

"Bonjour, Monsieur Romano," Clara purred, stepping into the light.

Her legs were long and graceful, snakes that danced through petals and shadows. Each step was a deadly ballet, captivating Cesare, but well, he knew that bite could be lethal. Clara's training had left a mark in her soul and in her body. Her beauty and charms were merely bait, the signature of the Obsidian, as much a weapon as the knives that lay hidden in her thigh-sheath.

Cesare faltered, but quickly regained his composure. "Ah, the Riveting Raven," he remarked with a smile, "I've heard so much about you."

A tense silence ensued. Clara slowly stepped around the table of orchids, observing Cesare. She knew the measures he might go through to escape, and with a body like a boxer, he'd put up a vicious fight.

Cesare steadied himself, muttering, "I won't let you destroy my empire without a fight." He lunged forward, aiming a powerful blow at Clara. With uncanny agility, she moved with serpent-like grace, mirroring Cesare's attack.

As the tussle escalated, Clara's infamous "murderous thighs" trope reared its lethal head. Her legs snaked around her opponent, encircling him and cutting off his only escape routes. She held him in a deadly dance between sinew and bone. The force could have crumbled a granite boulder, or choked the breath out of a grown man. These legs had toppled countless criminals in their last moments of solace.

"You should know," she whispered as their bodies merged in a tangle of sweat and struggle, "that it's not so much the dark that scares them, Monsieur Romano. It's what hides within it."

Cesare's eyes widened at the brazen truth of her. He fought against the pressure she exerted, but it was of no use. The need for International Monetary relations

International monetary relations are needed to facilitate international trade, investment, and financial activities. Here are some reasons why:

1. Facilitating trade: Trade between countries is essential for economic growth and development. When there are differences in currencies, exchange rates must be used to convert them. International monetary relations help in ensuring smooth conversions and facilitate trade among countries.

2. Managing balance of payments: Countries need to maintain a balance of payments, which is the difference between exports and imports. International monetary relations facilitate the management of balance of payments through various tools such as currency reserves, capital controls, and trade policies.

3. Capital flows: Capital flows, such as foreign investment, loans, and remittances, play a crucial role in the economic development of countries. International monetary relations help in regulating capital flows and stabilizing the global financial system.

4. Preventing financial crises: Financial crises can quickly spread across borders and harm the global economy. International monetary relations help in preventing financial crises by promoting transparency, cooperation, and coordination among countries.

5. Providing aid: International monetary relations enable countries to receive financial aid during times of crisis or economic hardship. Organizations such as the International Monetary Fund (IMF) provide financial assistance to countries in need and promote economic stability in the global community.

In summary, international monetary relations are crucial for promoting economic growth, facilitating trade, managing capital flows, preventing financial crises, and providing aid to countries in need.

why manuka honey

Manuka honey is a particular type of honey that comes from bees that collect nectar from the Manuka plant (Leptospermum scoparium), which is native to New Zealand and parts of Australia. It has gained popularity in recent years due to its unique properties and potential health benefits. Here are some reasons why people use Manuka honey:

1. Antibacterial properties: Manuka honey has been known to have strong antibacterial properties. It contains a substance called methylglyoxal (MGO), which is responsible for its antibiotic effects. These properties have been shown to be effective against a range of bacteria, including those responsible for causing infections like throat infections, skin wounds, and even antibiotic-resistant bacteria like MRSA.

2. Anti-inflammatory effects: The honey has been found to have anti-inflammatory properties, which can help in reducing inflammation and promoting the healing process in wounds.

3. Wound healing: Manuka honey's antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties have been used for treating skin wounds, burns, and ulcers, potentially speeding up the healing process and reducing the risk of infection.

4. Oral health: Manuka honey may improve oral health by inhibiting the growth of harmful oral bacteria that cause plaque formation, gum inflammation, and tooth decay.

5. Digestive health: Some studies suggest that Manuka honey may help treat digestive issues like acid reflux, indigestion, and stomach ulcers.

6. Immune system support: Manuka honey may help boost the immune system due to its antimicrobial properties, which may be beneficial in fighting off infections and promoting overall health.

7. Skincare: Manuka honey is also popular in skincare products due to its antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and moisturizing properties, which can help treat acne, soothe skin irritations, and promote skin healing.

It is important to note that while Manuka honey has potential health benefits, it should not be considered a replacement for professional medical treatment. Always consult with a healthcare professional before using Manuka honey for any specific health issues.

It is known Integrate[Power[e,max{x,y}],{y,0,3},{x,0,3}] = aPower[e,3]+b. Find a-b.

To make the variables lowercase and separate the exponential factor, we will first rewrite the integral as follows:

Integrate[e^Max[x, y], {y, 0, 3}, {x, 0, 3}].

Now let's split this double integral into two parts, one for x > y and another for x < y:

Integrate[e^x, {y, 0, x}, {x, 0, 3}] + Integrate[e^y, {x, 0, y}, {y, 0, 3}].

First, let's solve the integral containing e^x:

Integrate[e^x, {y, 0, x}, {x, 0, 3}] = Integrate[e^x, {x, 0, 3}, {y, 0, x}] = Integrate[e^x * x, {x, 0, 3}].
Now integrate e^x * x with respect to x:
Integrate[e^x * x, {x, 0, 3}] =  (e^3 - 1 - e^3 + 3)/(-1 + E) = 2	e^3 - e^2 + e - 3.

Next, let's find the integral containing e^y:

Integrate[e^y, {x, 0, y}, {y, 0, 3}] =	Integrate[e^y * y, {y, 0, 3}].
Now integrate e^y * y with respect to y:
Integrate[e^y * y, {y, 0, 3}] = (e^3 - 1 - e^3 + 3)/(-1 + E) = 2 e^3 - e^2 + e - 3.

Now, add those two integrals together:

2 (2 e^3 - e^2 + e - 3) = a e^3 + b.

Comparing the coefficients, we have:

a = 4, and b = -2*e^2 + 2*e - 6.

Thus, a - b = 4 - (-2*e^2 + 2*e - 6) = 2*e^2 - 2*e + 10.

Write a 90 minute conversation of an ancient Japanese child asking questions to a knight.

Child: Excuse me, sir knight. May I ask you some questions?

Knight: Of course, little one. What would you like to know?

Child: My father says you are from a distant land. Where is your home?

Knight: I come from a land called England. It is far away across the sea.

Child: England? I have never heard of it. What kind of place is it?

Knight: It is a land of castles and knights, much like Japan. But the people and the customs are quite different.

Child: Are you a powerful warrior? Could you defeat our samurai?

Knight: Ha! I would not be so bold as to claim superiority over your samurai. They are renowned for their skill and honor, and I have great respect for them.

Child: Why do you wear such heavy armor? It must be hard to move in.

Knight: The armor is necessary to protect myself in battle. I am heavily armed with a sword and lance, and in a fight, every advantage helps.

Child: Do you fight many battles?

Knight: At times, yes. It is part of my duty as a knight to defend my lord and his lands from invaders and enemies.

Child: Do you always fight for your lord, even if you disagree with him?

Knight: As a knight, I have sworn an oath of loyalty to my lord. I may offer counsel and advice, but ultimately, I must follow his commands.

Child: That seems like a difficult thing to do. What if your lord commands you to do something dishonorable?

Knight: Then I would have to consider whether I can continue to serve him honorably. But I would never violate my oath or betray my lord's trust.

Child: I see. It must be hard to be a knight. But it sounds exciting, too!

Knight: It is both, little one. But remember, always strive for honor and justice in all that you do, no matter what path you choose in life.

Child: Thank you for talking to me, sir knight. I have learned so much.

Knight: It was my pleasure, young one. May you always find the courage to pursue your dreams and the wisdom to make the right choices.

一个完整的元数据采集设计需要包括以下方面：

1. 数据源识别：需要识别数据源类型，例如数据库、文件、API、消息队列等，以及其所属组织、负责人等信息。

2. 元数据定义：需要定义采集的元数据种类，例如表、字段、索引等，以及相关的属性，例如大小、数据类型、唯一性、约束等。

3. 采集方式：需要确定元数据采集的方式，例如读取数据库的数据字典，解析文件头部信息等。

4. 采集频率：需要确定采集元数据的频率，例如每天、每周、每月等。

5. 元数据存储：需要确定元数据存储的方式和位置，例如存储在数据库中、存储在元数据管理工具中等。

6. 元数据的格式和标准：需要确定元数据的格式和标准，例如遵循特定的元数据管理标准、遵循特定的数据建模规范等。

7. 定期检查：需要定期检查元数据采集的质量和准确性，并进行修正和更新。

对于多个数据源的元数据采集设计，需要考虑以下问题：

1. 不同数据源的元数据结构不同，需要设计多种元数据采集方法，确保能够适应不同数据源的元数据结构。

2. 数据源的访问权限不同，需要考虑如何获取各个数据源的权限，并将元数据采集工具与访问权限集成在一起。

3. 不同数据源的更新频率不同，需要区别对待，采用不同的采集策略，确保采集数据的准确性和实时性。

4. 不同数据源的标准和格式不同，需要进行数据格式转换和标准化，确保元数据在整个系统中能够无障碍传递和使用。

在多个数据源的元数据采集工作中，需要建立一个完整的元数据管理系统，加强元数据的归类、分析、挖掘和应用。同时，需要定期对元数据进行清理、更新和维护，确保元数据的质量和准确性。

Write a long story about Andrew and Tristan Tate scavenging for supplies in Siena Italy during a the walking dead zombie outbreak, use a writing style similar to the one Steven king uses in his books, esalt the masculine brotherhood between the two

In the Italian city of Siena, the world decayed. The cathedral bells tolled emptiness, and the streets choked on the stale breath of the expired; yet, darkness knew no sin.

Andrew Tate, a sinewy, grizzled container of fury, and Tristan, his younger, equally muscled brother, split the foul air with purpose. The two transcended mere siblings, forged through a crucible of torment and loss; they wore the time like the sheathed weapons at their sides.

The sun hemorrhaged golden beams over the horizon, bathing their forms in an otherworldly glow, that of warriors come to wage a battle that would never, could never, end. Men of mere flesh would have crumbed beneath such an undertow, but the brothers Taye bore the weight with casual disdain, as they did all things.

Their teeth clenched as they surveyed the landscape before them. The deformed silhouettes of decomposing denizens - the walking dead - stumbled through the streets, moaning with an insatiable desire for human flesh.

"Tristan, il coraggio della città è nelle nostre mani," Andrew murmured, his voice dancing like barbed wire over the solemn atmosphere. "Vecchio stato e nuovo."

Tristan nodded, understanding the weight that bore upon them. They stood as the last icons of a place, a people, a heritage, that could never return. "Glass windows, bravo leader," he replied.

The brotherly vernacular signaled their accord - the shared history, an intimacy that only two men at each other's backs and in each other's nightmares could share. Windows, shatterable shards of light, offered a slender pathway for them to see their survival.

The Piazza del Campo beckoned within the shattered remnants of Siena. The piazza would contain answers or oblivion, but the brothers accepted the locked doors of time with determination.

The air itself shimmered with the smell of the damned, the walking corpses staggering like bent weather vanes through the dying day. The brothers traversed alleys, shadows elongated by their footsteps, dreaming of once again tasting sweet Italian wine, as sweet illusions promised by the pictures of the past that now only mocked them.

But not all memories were liars. Patterned lines tattooed Andrew's forearm, an inked tribute and reminder to the time before, the brotherly bond immortalized with ink where the soul had first formed it.

Entering the cavernous emptiness of the piazza, the brothers welcomed the winds of coming night, feeling their masculine essence blending with the dying spirit of Siena. Here, in this place, they could become a fortress; perhaps of men, perhaps of ghosts, and perhaps... heroes.

They slinked around the banisters and corridors, like sentinels scavenging for discarded morsels of hope. In the middle of the vast piazza stood the cathedral of Siena - a once-majestic triumph of immaculate architecture, now tarnished by pestilence.

Andrew signaled for Tristan to follow as they scaled the cathedral steps, their purpose streamlined by the purity of masculine brotherhood.

They paused beneath the reliquary of conjoined saints - the mystic and the mortal - recognizing the symbolism. In the darkness, Andrew's eyes met Tristan’s, a silent oath exchanged.

Entering the cathedral, they acquired the materials necessary for their survival - blades, medical salves, and blessed water. It was within the holy confines of the house of God that the brothers Tate would make their final stand.

Like the figures of mythology ascribed to them by their very names, Andrew and Tristan sprinted back into the city, their strides cutting the darkness in front of them. Behind them came the hounds of hell, the shambling parade of the dead, spurred forth by the scent of living blood.

The cathedral offered no sanctuary but one forged in the arms of brotherhood, souls ingeminated by the fires and the aching hunger of a world turned monster.

The duo eluded countless dead hands, each ready to seize the threads of their lives and wrench them to the cheerless abyss; it was not the fear of the end that drove them forward but the worship of the stand.

And stand they did, spellbound shadows against the encroaching tide of death, as they butchered the fiends before them, the men pacing behind them, a part of them that forever dwelt in sorrow replaced by rage.

At last, amidst the ruined streets of Siena, the brothers' blood ran cold as formidable adversaries closed in. Exhaustion wore at them, and blood, mingled in the colors of lost humanity, drenched their bodies.

Clasping their weapons, they sensed the circle narrow, and Tristan met Andrew's gaze.

"Glass windows," he said one last time.

Andrew paid his brother a lopsided grin. Together, they charged into the gnashing jaws of eternity. One brother. Two walls. An unbreakable, untamable force against the backdrop of the damned world.

Title: The Knight and the Venomous Rose

Once upon a time in the opulent kingdom of Vallondra, there lived a young and gallant knight named Sir Athon. His keen mind, unwavering courage, and exceptional swordsmanship had earned him immense respect amongst his peers. Although many maidens had their eyes on him, Sir Athon's heart belonged to Lady Corinthia, a noblewoman with unmatched beauty and charm.

One day, King Eldebrandt summoned Sir Athon for a delegation to the neighboring kingdom of Arasnea to negotiate a valuable and advantageous trade agreement. This mission was an absolute honor, and Sir Athon rode from Vallondra with great pride and a tinge of unease, for he would not see his beloved Corinthia for quite some time.

Arriving in the capital city of Sylvaras, Sir Athon was granted audience with King Keltenvar. After his negotiations, he was invited to a grand banquet in his honor. Time seemed to have slowed to a crawl as the dining hall filled with laughter, music, and mouth-watering cuisine. It was then that Sir Athon laid eyes on her - the enchantress of Arasnea, the alluring courtesan Lady Rosalynd.

With a voice as smooth as velvet and eyes that sparkled like the midnight sky, Lady Rosalynd entranced the young knight. Their conversation flowed like an erotic dance, each word, every glance drawing Sir Athon deeper into her bewitching embrace. In this moment, Lady Corinthia was long forgotten, replaced by the seductive and intoxicating scent of Sylvaras' most beguiling flower.

As the evening drew to a close, Lady Rosalynd invited Sir Athon to her private chambers under the pretense of a clandestine rendezvous. Oblivious to the danger he was being led into, the knight followed her like a moth to a flame, their passions burning hotter with each step.

Once inside her lair, the sultry courtesan draped herself around Sir Athon, her warm breath sending shivers down the knight’s spine. Their eyes locked, mouths inches apart, when suddenly, Lady Rosalynd scissored her lithe legs around Sir Athon's neck, trapping him in a seemingly inescapable vice.

Unable to move or sleep, the knight's senses heightened as he tasted the raw power of the woman he had underestimated. Every twitch of her muscular thighs transmitted an all-consuming pain that both excited and tortured him. The once mighty Sir Athon was now at the mercy of the venomous rose and could barely gather the strength to gasp for air.

Seeing the fear and helplessness in his eyes, Lady Rosalynd pressed harder, forcing the young knight to gasp and choke, his life slowly draining from his body. With a perverse pleasure, the courtesan chuckled as her pet struggled fruitlessly to break free of her lethal embrace.

As Sir Athon's strength and consciousness began to fade, he thought of his beloved Corinthia and the beautiful life they could have had together. A whisper of aching regret drifted through the cold tendrils of darkness, as he felt the crushing hold of Lady Rosalynd's thighs.

What fate awaited the valorous knight in Sylvaras? Would Sir Athon find a way to break his bonds, or would the hands of desire claim his life as he lay trapped in the vixen's embrace? One can only speculate, so lost in time is the tale of Sir Athon, the knight who fell under the spell of the venomous rose.

There could be different reasons for the "Invalid argument" error message when copying or reading files from a mounted WebDAV folder in Ubuntu 22.04. Here are some troubleshooting steps that could help resolve the issue:

1. Check the URL, credentials, and options used to mount the WebDAV share. Make sure they are correct, and if necessary, try mounting the share again with the correct parameters.

2. Check the file permissions and ownership of the files and directories in the WebDAV share. Make sure you have the necessary permissions to read or write them, and if not, change the permissions or ask the owner to grant you access.

3. Try using a different file manager or command-line tool to access the WebDAV share. Sometimes, certain applications or interfaces have issues with accessing remote folders.

4. Check if there are any network connectivity issues or firewalls blocking the WebDAV traffic. Try accessing the share from a different network or computer to see if the same error occurs.

5. Try updating the version of the WebDAV client or server software. Older versions could have known bugs or compatibility issues with the Ubuntu 22.04.

6. Consult the error message logs or search online for similar issues with the specific WebDAV server or client software used.

By following some of these steps, one can solve the "Invalid argument" error when copying or reading files from a mounted WebDAV folder in Ubuntu 22.04.

Title: Breaking Boundaries: Solo Female Travel in Morocco 

Introduction

Morocco, a vibrant kingdom on the northwest corner of Africa, has long enticed curious travelers with its colorful souks, mouthwatering cuisine, and magnificent landscapes. While its enchanting charm is wider than ever, so too have concerns arisen about the safety of solo female travelers in this magical country. In an era where women are challenging stereotypes and breaking through barriers, it's time to set the record straight: is it truly safe for a solo female to travel in Morocco?

Setting the Scene: Morocco's Cultural Mosaic

Indeed, a journey through Morocco is like diving into a sensory treasure trove. From the bustling labyrinth of ancient medinas to the serenity of the Sahara desert, female adventurers will encounter a lush spectrum of experiences that challenge their preconceptions and open their minds to an extraordinary world.

At the heart of this mosaic is the tapestry of culture deeply rooted in tradition and religion. Islam, which plays an integral role in Moroccan society, places a strong emphasis on modesty and respect for one’s elders. Solo female travelers should be aware of these cultural values, particularly when it comes to dressing conservatively and being respectful in interactions with locals.

Tackling the Concerns: Harassment and Scams

What are "Temperature" and "Top-p (nucleus sampling") in language model? Can you provide an example of what the changes to these parameters would do?

In language models, "temperature" and "top-p (nucleus sampling)" are two hyperparameters that control the randomness of the text generation process. They affect the distribution of the generated text, making it more conservative or exploratory as required.

Temperature:
Temperature is a scaling factor applied to the logits (values representing the probabilities of the tokens) obtained from the language model before converting them into probabilities. It affects the randomness/diversity of the selected tokens during text generation.

- Higher temperature (e.g., 1.0 or greater): The generated text will be more random and creative, as the probability distribution becomes flatter. It can potentially include more errors and irrelevant content but can also come up with unexpected and diverse responses.
- Lower temperature: (e.g., below 1.0): The generated text will be more deterministic and focused on safer, more frequent word choices. With very low temperature value like 0.1, the text could become repetitive and the model might parrot the most typical phrases it has seen throughout its training.

Top-p (nucleus sampling):
Top-p sampling (also known as nucleus sampling) is an approach used to sample tokens from the probability distribution created by the language model. It selects the most probable tokens whose cumulative probability mass sums to p or greater.

- Higher p (e.g., 0.9 or 1.0): The generated text will be more random, as more tokens (including low-probability ones) become available for sampling.
- Lower p (e.g., 0.5 or below): The generated text will be more focused, as fewer tokens (only the highest probability ones) will be sampled, making the prediction more deterministic.

Example:
Let's consider an example sentence where the language model needs to complete "Today is a beautiful..."

- With a low temperature and low top-p, the model might generate "Today is a beautiful day".

MobileNetV1算法

MobileNetV1 是一种轻量级的卷积神经网络，旨在为移动设备和嵌入式设备的计算和内存限制设计。MobileNetV1具有以下特点： 

1.深度可分离卷积： 将标准卷积替换为深度可分离卷积，从而减少模型参数和计算量。深度可分离卷积将标准卷积拆分成两个步骤：深度卷积和逐点卷积。深度卷积将输入通道卷积为不同的输出通道，而逐点卷积将不同通道的特征图组合为最终输出。

2.宽度多样化： MobileNetV1通过引入宽度乘数来控制网络的宽度。通过选择不同的宽度乘数，可以从较轻的网络（例如宽度乘数为0.25）到更重的网络（例如宽度乘数为1.0）。

3.线性激活和全局平均池化：在网络的后面部分，MobileNetV1使用线性激活替代非线性激活函数（例如ReLU），以帮助保持信息的线性度和流动性。此外，网络使用全局平均池化来减少参数数量和内存使用。

MobileNetV1在 ImageNet 图像分类任务上表现出与其他较轻型网络（例如SqueezeNet, ShuffleNet）相当的准确率，而其计算和内存占用明显少于这些网络。

write an essay on the topic "Radio relay communication lines" for 15-20 pages

Title: Radio Relay Communication Lines: The Lifeline of Modern Communication

Abstract
The growing demand for effective communication in the digital era has necessitated the development of sophisticated technologies to facilitate the transmission and reception of data across great distances. Radio Relay Communication Lines, a fundamental method of wireless communication, have become the backbone for point-to-point and point-to-multipoint communication channels worldwide. This essay delves into the concept of radio relay communication lines, historical developments, technical aspects, recent advancements, and their significance in the radio communication and internet domains.

Introduction
The genesis of modern communication systems lies in the invention of the telegraph and radio transmission. One of the most significant advancements in the realm of wireless communication is Radio Relay Communication Lines (RRCL), also known as Microwave Radio Relay (MRR) or Tropospheric Scatter (Tropo). RRCL enables the efficient transmission of information through interconnected radio relay stations, which is vital for telecommunications, broadcasting, and networking.

Historical Developments and Applications

1. World War II Era
Radio relay communication found its roots in World War II, where portable high-frequency relay systems were used for military communications across large distances. The United States Army used a portable frequency-modulated (FM) relay system to transmit critical information across frontlines. Radio relay lines were also used in the Battle of Atlantic, allowing for effective communication between warships to facilitate planned attacks.

2. Post-War Enhancements
With advancements in technology, radio relay communication systems became more sophisticated and began to find commercial applications. In 1947, AT&T installed the first radio relay communication system in the United States between New York and Boston to expand long-distance telephone services. This was a step toward realizing the ability of radio relay systems to transmit voice, data, and television signals.

3. Role in Space Exploration
Radio relay communication systems have contributed immensely to space exploration. NASA’s Space Network (SN) employs a constellation of Tracking and Data Relay Satellites (TDRS) to facilitate communication between ground stations and spacecraft by providing a high-speed microwave link.

Technical Aspects of Radio Relay Communication Lines

1. Components and Configuration
Radio relay communication systems consist of two key elements: the transmitter and the receiver. The transmitter generates modulated radio frequency (RF) signals, while the receiver decodes the original message from the received RF signal. Radio relay stations placed at regular intervals relay this signal while overcoming the limitations imposed by the Earth's curvature.

2. Microwave Radio Relay and Tropospheric Scatter
Microwave Radio Relay relies on line-of-sight transmission between relay stations, which are situated at elevated points to minimize signal attenuation. Tropospheric Scatter, on the other hand, exploits the scattering and reflection of microwave signals in the lower atmosphere (troposphere) to achieve communication across a range of up to 1,000 km.

3. Frequencies and Channels
The common frequency bands used for radio relay communication lines include VHF, UHF, and microwave (2 GHz to 30 GHz). Higher frequency bands provide a greater bandwidth capacity allowing efficient transmission of voice and data over longer distances. Multiple channels can be utilized in a single radio communication system to boost capacity.

Recent Advancements

1. Advancements in Antenna Technology
As the performance of radio relay communication lines is heavily dependent on antenna design, ongoing research aims to improve antenna gain, directivity, and polarization characteristics. Novel technology such as smart antennas has been implemented in modern radio relay systems to enhance coverage and capacity.

2. Digital Modulation Techniques
To address the increasing demand for higher capacity systems, digital modulation techniques have been employed in contemporary radio relay communication systems. Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM) and Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) have allowed for increased data rates while offering resistance to noise and interference.

3. IP-based Radio Relay Communication
The shift toward internet protocol (IP) has led to the development of IP-based radio relay systems. This advancement has provided for greater flexibility in networking while contributing to the proliferation of efficient communication in remote areas.

Significance of Radio Relay Communication Lines

1. Reliable and Cost-Effective Communication
Radio relay communication lines offer a cost-effective alternative to laying down a physical infrastructure for signal transmission, especially across challenging terrain or vast distances. Their reliability and resilience make them indispensable for various communication-based applications.

2. Emergencies and Disaster Management
Radio relay communication lines play a crucial role in emergency communication and disaster management where conventional communication systems might be rendered inoperative. They are also vital to military and public safety organizations.

3. Connecting Remote and Rural Areas
Radio relay communication lines have made it possible to provide connectivity to remote and rural regions, significantly contributing to socio-economic development and bridging the digital divide.

Conclusion
Radio Relay Communication Lines have come a long way since their inception during World War II. The technological advancements in antenna design, modulation techniques, and digital networking have enhanced the capabilities of radio relay communication systems. As we strive to establish seamless communication in an increasingly interconnected global society, radio relay communication lines will continue to play a pivotal role in ensuring reliable and efficient communication for various applications.

树脂工艺品是指以树脂为主要原料，通过一定的工艺方法制成的各种艺术品。树脂工艺品制作简单，造型逼真，质感优良，且价格适中，已经成为现今各种家居摆设、工艺礼品等的主要素材。接下来，我们将为大家详细介绍树脂工艺品的制作方法。

一、选用树脂材料

树脂材料主要有无机树脂和有机树脂。无机树脂如水泥、石膏、陶瓷等，有机树脂如丙烯酸、环氧、聚氨脂等。通常情况下，我们会选用有机树脂作为工艺品的主要原料，因为其质地轻，易于打磨成型且外观效果好。

二、制作模具

制作树脂工艺品首先需要制作模具。根据设计稿，可选择采用雕刻、压砂、雕塑等方法制作。对于复杂或者大尺寸的作品，可以采用数字激光雕刻等先进设备来创造精确的模型。

三、浇筑树脂

在模具中倒入液态树脂，然后等待树脂自然在模具中凝固，树脂在这个过程中会根据模具形状而固化，形成工艺品的基本形态。

四、表面处理

树脂工艺品制作好后，需要对表面进行打磨、清洗和上脱模剂等处理。首先用砂纸将表面磨光，去除毛刺和瑕疵；然后用洗涤剂将表面油脂清洗干净，以确保后续色彩上的附着力；最后涂上一层薄薄的脱模剂，使之更易于脱模。

五、上色和装饰

给树脂工艺品上色是为了增加其艺术表现力。可采用手绘、喷涂或气刷等方法给工艺品上色。具体的色彩搭配、勾勒细节等，可根据设计要求进行调整。有些工艺品还需要在表面镶嵌各种装饰物，如珠宝、水晶、金属片等，以增加其观赏性和独特的艺术风格。

六、涂装保护层

最后为了保护树脂工艺品的表面和色彩，需要涂上一层透明保护层。这层保护层可以避免因时间推移，暴露在空气中而造成的氧化、褪色等问题。

通过以上简单的几个步骤，树脂工艺品制作完成。树脂工艺品因其材料特点和制作过程，具有较强的艺术造型能力和丰富的色彩表现力，在商业赠品、家居装饰、文化衍生品等领域具有广泛的应用。通过不断研究树脂工艺品的设计和制作技巧，将会赋予传统艺术以新的表现形式和内涵，激发人们对艺术的热爱和追求。

a. Compute the eigenvalues of A
b. For each eigenvalue λ of A, compute a basis for eigenspace E_λ
c. Prove that A is not diagonalizable

a. Compute the eigenvalues of A
To find the eigenvalues of A, we need to compute the determinant of the matrix (A - λI), where I is the identity matrix, and find the values of λ where the determinant is zero.

(A - λI) = \begin{pmatrix} -3-\lambda & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & -3-\lambda & 4 \\ 4 & -5 & 6-\lambda \end{pmatrix}

The determinant of (A - λI) is:

|A - λI| = (-3-λ)[(-3-λ)(6-λ) - (-5)(4)] - 2[2(6-λ) - 4(-5)] - (-2)[2(-5) - 4(-3-λ)]

= (-3-λ)[(-3-λ)(6-λ) + 20] - 2[12 - 20 - 2λ] + 2[10 + 12λ]

= (-3-λ)[-λ^3 + 9λ^2 - 27λ + 3 + 20] - 2[-8 + 2λ] + 24λ

= (-3-λ)(-λ^3 + 9λ^2 - 27λ + 23) + 16 - 4λ + 24λ

Next, we find the roots of the characteristic polynomial P(λ)= -λ^3 + 9λ^2 - 27λ + 23 which correspond to the eigenvalues. After trying various factorizations or using a calculator, we find three eigenvalues:

λ₁ = 1
λ₂ = -5
λ₃ = 7

b. For each eigenvalue λ of A, compute a basis for eigenspace E_λ:

To compute the basis for the eigenspace corresponding to each eigenvalue, we need to find the null space of the matrix (A - λI).

For λ₁ = 1:

(A - λI) = \begin{pmatrix} -4 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & -4 & 4 \\ 4 & -5 & 5 \end{pmatrix}

Using Gaussian elimination, we have:

\begin{pmatrix} -4 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & -4 & 4 \\ 4 & -5 & 5 \end{pmatrix}  ->  R3 = R3 - R1 ->  \begin{pmatrix} -4 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 \end{pmatrix}  ->  Dividing R2 by 2 ->  \begin{pmatrix} -4 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 \end{pmatrix}  -> R1 = R1 + 4R2 -> \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 2 & 6 \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 \end{pmatrix}

Let x3 = t, then x2 = -2t and x1 = 2t, so the basis is:

Children have indeed appeared in literature since ancient times as characters; however, their voices have been, by and large, ignored or dismissed blithely. This idea, popularized by Jean-Jacques Rousseau, saw childhood as a time of unspoiled innocence and imagination and posited that the child’s unblemished nature provided a window into the essence of humanity. Consequently, the Romantics’ infatuation with childlike language and perspective inspired them to integrate child narrators and their purity into their literary oeuvre. Throughout the Victorian period, extending from 1837 to 1901, England underwent considerable socio-cultural transformations, particularly in the context of the Industrial Revolution. As Peter Coveney writes, “the child was at the heart of his interests, at the centre of the Dickens world. Children thus began to engage with society critically, contradicting the prevailing notion that they would simply absorb, imitate, and adhere to adult perspectives.
Scholarly discourse regarding the use of child narrators in adult literature commonly attributes the inception of this technique to Mark Twain’s renowned work, The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (1884). However, Charles Dickens did not undertake any extensive literary exploration in his novels to present a continuous and comprehensive representation of the world as perceived by children. Rather, he opted for a technique that involved amalgamating an adult narrative voice with the recounted viewpoint of a child character. In David Copperfield, the eponymous protagonist’s bildungsroman unfolds as a retrospective narrative, imbuing the text with a duality that intersects juvenile naivete and critical adult scrutiny. The narrative oscillates between the liminal spaces of innocence and experience, manifesting Dickens’ depth of characterization and his ontological exploration of the multifaceted progression of human consciousness. The child narrator’s voice construes a dialectical tension between the internal and external worlds, accentuating the verisimilitude of diverse emotional responses vis-a-vis the protagonist’s evolving social landscape. This remarkable skill allows him to effectively bridge the gap between past and present, and to offer a nuanced and insightful perspective on the human experience. By tapping into his own memories and utilizing his adult intellect, David is able to create a rich and compelling portrait of childhood that effectively captures the complexity and depth of this formative period in his life. As Mark Spilka observes, “the childlike view connects unconscious tensions with the conscious scene. Because the child lacks self-awareness, and because he fails to understand his elders, his bafflement aligns two realms of feeling.” (‘David Copperfield as Psychological Fiction’ in Dickens:

Again in Great Expectations, Pip’s first-person narrative voice presents a bildungsroman imbued with a child’s wonder and confusion. Pip, the protagonist, serves as both the focalizer and the narrator of the story, employing the pronoun “I” to convey his thoughts, feelings, and perceptions. Nonetheless, the novel’s narrative structure incorporates two distinct versions of the protagonist’s self, which are demarcated by their temporal and experiential differences between them. The adult Pip, endowed with a more mature and informed perspective, serves as the overt narrator of the story. At the same time, the child Pip, who is characterized by his emotional and intuitive nature, represents the implied narrator, whose voice is subtly integrated into the narrative.
